key_insight: Test-time scaling does not have to rely on fully independent samples. QuasiMoTTo shows that carefully designed correlated samplers can reduce redundant generations while still producing exact samples, making inference compute more efficient.
problem_solved: Language models often improve by generating many parallel attempts at inference time, but independent sampling wastes compute on near-duplicate outputs. This paper addresses the inefficiency of redundant parallel sampling during test-time scaling.
method: Introduces quasi-Monte Carlo style sampling for test-time scaling in language models.
Uses correlated, structured sample generation instead of independent attempts to cover the solution space more efficiently.
Aims to preserve exactness while improving diversity and reducing wasted inference compute.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could lower the cost of high-quality inference by making parallel sampling more efficient. It is especially relevant for tasks where many test-time attempts are used to boost accuracy, reliability, or reasoning performance.
visual_elements: Side-by-side pipeline showing independent sampling vs quasi-Monte Carlo sampling

Bar chart comparing accuracy vs inference cost
Icon set for compute, diversity, and exactness
paper_authors: Michael Y. Li, Anthony Zhan, Kanishk Gandhi, Noah D. Goodman, Emily B. Fox
